A_target.statement:
Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \R^n$ be a [[Definition:Curve|curve]].
The [[Definition:Length of Curve|length]] of $\gamma$ is:
:$\displaystyle \map L \gamma = \sup_P \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \norm {\map \gamma {t_i} - \map \gamma {t_{i - 1} } }$
where the [[Definition:Supremum of Set|supremum]] is over all [[Definition:Finite Subdivision|subdivisions]] $P = \set {a = t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_k = b}$.
If $\gamma$ is [[Definition:Continuously Differentiable|continuously differentiable]], then:
:$\displaystyle \map L \gamma = \int_a^b \norm {\map {\gamma'} t} \rd t$

B_source.statement:
Let $P$ be a [[Definition:Polygonal Path|polygonal path]] with [[Definition:Vertex of Polygon|vertices]] $p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_k$.
Then the [[Definition:Length of Curve|length]] of $P$ is:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \norm {p_i - p_{i - 1} }$

substitutions.the vertices of the polygon: the sample points of a partition of the parameter interval
substitutions.the finite sum of segment lengths: the approximating sum for a given partition
substitutions.refining the polygon: refining the partition, with mesh tending to zero

object_map.reformulation: Replace the curve by an inscribed polygon, so a continuous length becomes a finite sum, then refine.

validity_conditions: Refining a partition can only increase the approximating sum, by the triangle inequality, so the supremum is also the limit as the mesh tends to zero.
The curve is rectifiable exactly when that supremum is finite, which is the definition rather than a theorem.
For a continuously differentiable curve the mean value theorem converts each chord into a speed times a subinterval length, so the sums become Riemann sums for the integral of the speed.
proof_plan:
Let $P = \set {t_0, t_1, \ldots, t_k}$ be a [[Definition:Finite Subdivision|subdivision]] of $\closedint a b$.
The points $\map \gamma {t_i}$ are the vertices of an inscribed [[Definition:Polygonal Path|polygonal path]] of length $\displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k \norm {\map \gamma {t_i} - \map \gamma {t_{i - 1} } }$.

Let $Q$ be a [[Definition:Refinement of Subdivision|refinement]] of $P$ obtained by inserting $s \in \openint {t_{i - 1} } {t_i}$.
From the [[Triangle Inequality]]:
:$\norm {\map \gamma {t_i} - \map \gamma {t_{i - 1} } } \le \norm {\map \gamma {t_i} - \map \gamma s} + \norm {\map \gamma s - \map \gamma {t_{i - 1} } }$
so refining does not decrease the polygonal length.

Define $\map L \gamma$ as the [[Definition:Supremum of Set|supremum]] of these lengths over all subdivisions.
$\gamma$ is [[Definition:Rectifiable Curve|rectifiable]] {{iff}} $\map L \gamma < \infty$.

Let $\gamma$ be [[Definition:Continuously Differentiable|continuously differentiable]].
By the [[Mean Value Theorem]] applied to each coordinate, each segment length is approximately $\norm {\map {\gamma'} {\xi_i} } \paren {t_i - t_{i - 1} }$.
Thus the polygonal lengths are [[Definition:Riemann Sum|Riemann sums]] for $\norm {\gamma'}$, and:
:$\displaystyle \map L \gamma = \int_a^b \norm {\map {\gamma'} t} \rd t$
{{qed}}
